title: An indexed process wiki with just-in-time reading
status: in progress (product owner priority D170, one-card stop-the-line waiver)

intent.line: Intent: the product owner wants the process split into small pages, each with a one-line summary, under one index, so that each seat reads only the pages its role and step need and the facilitator keeps its state in the wiki and handoff notes, without any rule losing its decision anchor. In the words of D170: "card 234 ('An indexed process wiki with just-in-time reading') is the highest priority." and, for the reason, "Every turn re-reads the whole context, so fresh seats overpay by reading everything and the long facilitator session overpays on every turn; the wiki cuts both and gives the product owner one readable place for the whole process." The card text adds: "rules keep their decision anchors and history; the decisions index still builds; the checks still read the rules" (Invariants) and "a seat that misses a rule because it did not read a page it needed is recorded as a counter-metric case" (Fails with). Criterion 1 is the first Done check: the process is split into indexed pages with one-line summaries, and every rule still resolves to its decision; the adopted condition of window 234-taskforce makes it git-checkable (numbers and measurement methods present, every decision anchor resolving from its wiki page).
sources: D170 in docs/decisions/process-and-staffing.md (product owner ruling 2026-11-01: highest priority, one-card stop-the-line waiver)

stand_downs.adjustment: GREEN PROOF BLOCK AND A FLOOR (for criterion 2 and the cycles after it). (1) Every green commit body, from a scanned or an unscanned seat, carries a block 'Proof': (a) a plan table with a row 'caller: <file:line>, or <owner and hash to come>' for each check built; (b) the mutations the green ran, each with command and red/green result, or 'none run', which counts as a miss; (c) for a seat with no command source, the deleted-line count from git show --numstat and the one command that ran the checker on the real repository with its exit code. (2) The checker gets a floor: criterion 2's red adds a test that fails when docs/process-wiki holds fewer rule lines citing a decision anchor than a share of the bullet rules in TEAM_WORKING_AGREEMENT.md, or lacks a page for a seat role of the task force; the architect sets the share in the criterion 2 slice, not the green. (3) The facilitator returns a green body with no Proof block before the record commit. Metric: built checks with no caller outside tests and no owner, plus green bodies without the Proof block (now 1 + 1 = 2; target 0 at the criterion 2 green), reported with wiki rule coverage (now 4 of 128, 3.1 percent) and mutations run by the green (now 0). Counter-metrics: (a) red-to-green minutes (now 9.75; card 227 41.4 and 31.4; limit 60) and commit size against D136 (green 6 files, 274 lines; limits 15 files, 400 lines): a rise means the block pads the body or the floor bloats the green; (b) rule lines copied into the wiki to meet the floor and then missed by a seat: counted in rule_miss_cases (now 0 recorded; its source named); (c) minutes from green to the facilitator's record (now 1 min 22 s). Goodhart guard: a caller counts only if the Proof block shows its output on a real repository, and the floor counts rule lines that cite a decision anchor, not lines of prose.
